common_patterns.overview: Reusable Playwright patterns for common debugging scenarios. These patterns cover auth flows, control flows, visual regression, console debugging, REST API verification, and accessibility audits.

pattern.name: auth_flow_debugging
pattern.description: Debug broken authentication flows including login forms, OAuth redirects, token management, and session persistence.

step.title: Navigate to Login Page
step.code: await page.goto('https://example.com/login', { waitUntil: 'networkidle' }); await page.screenshot({ path: 'evidence/auth-flow/01-login-page.png' });

step.title: Submit Credentials
Capture Redirect Chain
Verify Session State
step.validation: Check that: - Cookies include session/auth tokens - No console errors related to auth - Network request to /api/auth/login returned 200 - Redirect landed on expected dashboard URL

debugging_heuristics.heuristic: If login button click does nothing → check for disabled button state, hidden form fields, or JavaScript event handler failure.
If redirect fails or shows error → capture the intermediate URL. The redirect endpoint may return error HTML instead of redirecting.
If token is missing from cookies/localStorage → check the API response for the token payload. The server may not be sending it correctly.

pattern.name: visual_regression_detection
pattern.description: Compare two versions of a page to detect unintended visual changes. Useful after CSS changes, component updates, or dependency upgrades.

step.title: Capture Baseline
Capture Candidate
Extract CSS Differences
Verify Screenshots via Vision
step.description: Use Qwen3.6 Abliterated vision capabilities to read both screenshots and identify visual differences that computed styles may miss (layout shifts, overlapping elements, missing images).

pattern.name: rest_api_flow_verification
pattern.description: Verify REST API call flows end-to-end, including request payloads, response bodies, status codes, and header propagation.

step.title: Set Up Network Interception
Trigger the API Flow
Validate Request/Response Chain

debugging_heuristics.heuristic: If a POST returns 4xx → capture request payload and check Content-Type header. Missing JSON Content-Type is a common cause.
If redirect happens without API call → the flow may be using server-side rendering instead of client-side API calls. Check for form action URLs.
If response body is empty → check if the endpoint requires specific headers (Authorization, Accept) that are not being sent.

pattern.name: user_interaction_debugging
pattern.description: Debug complex user interaction sequences: dropdowns, scrolling, theming, modals, drag-and-drop, infinite scroll, and multi-step forms.

subpattern.name: dropdown_interaction
subpattern.description: Verify dropdown menus open, display options, and handle selection

steps.step: 3. Wait for menu animation (waitForSelector or fixed delay)
5. Verify options are visible and correctly positioned
8. Verify the selected value appears in the trigger element

common_issues.issue: Dropdown opens but options are off-screen → check z-index and overflow: hidden on parent
Dropdown closes immediately → click event may be bubbling to a parent handler
Options are not clickable → element may be overlapped by another element

subpattern.name: scrolling_behavior
subpattern.description: Debug scroll-based UI issues: sticky headers, infinite scroll, scroll-triggered animations

steps.step: 4. Verify sticky elements remain in viewport
5. Check for infinite scroll loading indicator

subpattern.name: theming_verification
subpattern.description: Verify theme toggle and CSS custom property application

steps.step: 2. Extract CSS custom property values via page.evaluate()
3. Trigger theme toggle (click button, toggle switch)
7. Compare intended vs actual values for both themes

expected_comparison.theme: --bg-color: expected #ffffff → actual computed value --text-color: expected #000000 → actual computed value
--bg-color: expected #1a1a1a → actual computed value --text-color: expected #ffffff → actual computed value

pattern.name: console_error_investigation
pattern.description: Investigate JavaScript console errors that correlate with visual or functional bugs on the page.

step.title: Capture All Console Output
Filter and Categorize
Correlate with Visual State
step.description: For each error/warning, determine: - Does it occur during page load? (baseline issue) - Does it occur after a specific action? (interaction issue) - Does it correlate with a visual defect? (rendering issue) - Is it a known browser issue? (vendor bug)

step.title: Inject Debug Script
step.note: Only inject when standard console capture is insufficient. Overriding built-in functions can change behavior.

pattern.name: control_flow_automation
pattern.description: Automate multi-step control flows that require sequential decisions: wizard forms, multi-tab workflows, conditional branching, state machines.

step.title: Map the Control Flow
step.description: Before automating, map the expected flow: - Decision points (if X, go to step A; else step B) - State transitions (page1 → page2 → confirmation) - Error paths (validation error → stay on same page)

step.title: Execute with Branch Capture
Verify State Machine
step.description: Confirm that: - Each state transition produces the expected UI - Error states display correct messages - Back/forward navigation doesn't break state - Browser history is correctly managed

pattern.name: cross_browser_comparison
pattern.description: Compare rendering across Chromium, Firefox, and WebKit to identify browser-specific visual bugs.

step.title: Capture on Chromium (baseline)
Analyze Differences
step.description: Use Qwen3.6 Abliterated vision to compare screenshots across browsers. Look for: - Font rendering differences - Layout shift differences - Missing/extra elements - Color/theme differences

pattern.name: accessibility_audit
pattern.description: Perform a comprehensive accessibility audit focusing on human readability, WCAG contrast ratios, typography, and visual polish. This pattern addresses the critical gap between DOM visibility (Playwright's offsetParent check) and actual human readability.

prerequisites.prerequisite: Browser context is clean (no cached state)
Viewport set to target size (desktop or mobile)

step.title: Extract Contrast Ratios for All Text
step.validation: All body text must pass WCAG AA (4.5:1). Large text (≥22px) must pass 3:1. Effective contrast (ratio × opacity) is the true measure — an element at 50% opacity with 4.5:1 contrast has only 2.25:1 effective contrast.

step.title: Check Font Legibility

thresholds.threshold: Text below 14px is hard to read

step.title: Check Opacity/Alpha Transparency
step.note: Opacity is a contrast multiplier. An element at 75% opacity with 4.5:1 raw contrast has only 3.375:1 effective contrast — below the 4.5:1 WCAG AA threshold.

step.title: Check Color Blindness Safety
step.validation: Status indicators that rely solely on color (no text/icon) must be distinguishable under deuteranopia simulation. Red/green status indicators are the most common failure.

step.title: Check Layout and Visual Polish

visual_polish_criteria.criterion: Margins should be consistent within 10px across similar elements
h1 ≥ h2 ≥ h3 in font size; each level should be visually distinct
Cards and interactive elements should use consistent border-radius and box-shadow
Empty areas larger than 100x100px without content are dead space
Elements with overflow:hidden should not truncate text without ellipsis

step.title: Mobile Verification

mobile_criteria.criterion: No horizontal overflow at any breakpoint
Text should not overflow containers at mobile breakpoints
Elements should stack vertically without horizontal overflow

scoring.metric: Score 1.0 if all text passes WCAG AA, 0.5 if 80% pass, 0.0 if <80%
Score 1.0 if all text ≥ 14px with line-height ≥ 1.4
Score 1.0 if all elements with opacity < 0.8 have effective contrast ≥ 4.5
Score 1.0 if all color-only indicators pass deuteranopia simulation
Score 1.0 if alignment, typography, borders, and overflow are consistent

grade.grade: Excellent — all text is highly readable
Fair — some text is hard to read
Critical — most text is nearly invisible

pattern.name: color_design_audit
pattern.description: Perform a comprehensive color design audit covering dark-theme anti-patterns, WCAG contrast compliance, status indicator visibility, palette coherence, and color hierarchy. This pattern proactively detects common dark design mistakes WITHOUT being told what's wrong — it automatically flags issues like black text on dark backgrounds, pure white text causing glare, invisible status dots, and inconsistent palette lightness steps.

prerequisites.prerequisite: Browser context is clean (no cached state)
Viewport set to target size (desktop default)

step.title: Extract All Color Pairs
Compute WCAG Contrast and Apply Correct Threshold
Flag Dark Theme Anti-Patterns
Evaluate Palette Coherence and Hierarchy

palette_criteria.criterion: Background lightness should increase in 5-20% steps for surface hierarchy
Body text should be off-white (200-230 range) in dark mode, not pure white
Limit accent colors to primary + danger + success + warning; flag more than 4-5
Neutral greys should contain 2-5% brand hue tint for visual warmth

step.title: Generate Color Design Scorecard

scoring.metric: Score 1.0 if all text passes WCAG AA, 0.5 if 80% pass, 0.0 if <80%
Score 1.0 if no anti-patterns detected, -0.2 per violation
Score 1.0 if all indicators ≥ 3:1 contrast and include icon/text
Score 1.0 if lightness steps consistent, body text off-white, accents limited
Score 1.0 if semantic colors match dark-mode reference values

grade.grade: Excellent — color design is professional and accessible
Critical — most color choices violate best practices
